video_title: Lawfare Daily: Sander Tordoir on Europe's Strategic Choices
gist: Peter Harrell interviews CER chief economist Sander Tordoir on Europe's hawkish China pivot: a 350,000-unit quota on Chinese hybrid cars (vs ~1M run rate) to be replicated in chemicals and machine tools, a new Franco-German deterrence tool due in ~6 months, and an FDI-conditioning Industrial Accelerator Act. Tordoir cites 250K lost EU manufacturing jobs, Germany shedding 10-15K a month, and argues US tariffs were a footnote while transatlantic decoupling is infeasible.

themes.theme: EU-China hybrid car deal and new trade tools

insights.claim: The EU-China deal centers on an effective 350,000-unit quota on Chinese hybrid car exports to the EU versus a current run rate of about 1 million, with presumably prohibitive tariffs above the quota.
insights.speaker: Sander Tordoir
insights.so_what: Chinese automakers' EU hybrid volumes face a roughly 65% cap.
insights.quote: an effective quota on Chinese hybrid car exports to the EU of 350,000 cars, uh which compared to a current run rate of 1 million cars is a substantial reduction

insights.claim: China declined voluntary export restraints and instead let the EU impose a safeguard-style measure, which will in principle apply globally but in practice target China with open quotas for other partners.
insights.speaker: Sander Tordoir
insights.so_what: Expect safeguard/tariff-rate-quota mechanics as the EU's preferred template.

insights.claim: The October 5 Franco-German paper calling for a tougher China line gave Trade Commissioner Šefčovič credibility he otherwise lacked heading into talks with Wang Wentao.
insights.speaker: Sander Tordoir
insights.so_what: Franco-German alignment is the key enabler of tougher EU trade action.

insights.claim: Germany, long the EU's 'hesitator-in-chief' on China, has moved, and the German Chancellor now calls the renminbi 30% undervalued.
insights.speaker: Sander Tordoir
insights.so_what: German policy shift removes the main brake on EU trade defense.

insights.claim: The EU plans to replicate the hybrid tariff-rate-quota model in chemicals, machine tools and possibly legacy semiconductors where Chinese imports are surging.
insights.speaker: Sander Tordoir
insights.so_what: EU sectoral quotas could hit Chinese exporters in chemicals and machinery next.

insights.claim: EU leaders agreed to build a Franco-German 'second strike' deterrence tool within roughly six months, a narrower, easier-to-trigger alternative to the Anti-Coercion Instrument, which Tordoir calls a bazooka with a faulty trigger.
insights.speaker: Sander Tordoir
insights.so_what: A usable EU retaliation instrument may exist by around mid-2027.
insights.quote: It's a it's a bazooka which has a very faulty trigger.

insights.claim: Whether the new EU deterrence tool covers services, not just goods, will determine whether it could also be used against the US by hitting tech and financial services exports.
insights.speaker: Sander Tordoir
insights.so_what: Watch the services scope as a signal of risk to US tech exporters in Europe.

insights.claim: Tordoir expects France to push for services in the tool's scope and Germany for a narrower goods focus, and argues a focused instrument with a clear 'blast radius' is more likely to actually be used.
insights.speaker: Sander Tordoir
insights.so_what: A narrow goods-only tool is the more probable outcome.

insights.claim: Šefčovič and Wang Wentao are scheduled to meet again around January, and ECB President Lagarde, the Eurogroup president and Commissioner Dombrovskis have begun discussing currency imbalances with Chinese counterparts.
insights.speaker: Sander Tordoir
insights.so_what: EU-China currency diplomacy is at an early stage.

insights.claim: Under the deal Europe committed to keep delivering dual-use goods such as legacy ASML lithography machines and aircraft parts, while China committed to more predictable rare earth deliveries, though in practice China is slow-walking rare earths to Europe and the US.
insights.speaker: Sander Tordoir
insights.so_what: Rare-earth supply to European industry remains at risk despite paper commitments.

insights.claim: Tordoir argues Europe's sharply reduced exports to China, especially Germany's, leave Beijing little to retaliate on except supply chain warfare, which would be a dramatic escalation.
insights.speaker: Sander Tordoir
insights.so_what: EU trade measures carry lower retaliation risk than in the past.

insights.claim: Tordoir disagrees with Europe's choice to wall off supply-chain leverage: he argues the EU should have reminded China of its own chokepoints in semiconductors, aircraft and specialty chemicals like BASF, making trade tools less ambitious than they should be.
insights.speaker: Sander Tordoir
insights.so_what: EU trade defense is deliberately under-powered.

insights.claim: Tordoir argues China's export glut is a macro shock driven by weak domestic demand, an undervalued currency and broad industrial policy, warranting a broad US Section 301-style tariff response rather than sector-by-sector measures.
insights.speaker: Sander Tordoir
insights.so_what: Narrow measures won't stem the overall Chinese export surge.

insights.claim: The US-China supply chain truce on rare earths versus US export controls was originally set to end in early November and has been pushed to January.
insights.speaker: Peter Harrell
insights.so_what: A January deadline is a near-term US-China risk event.

insights.claim: The EU lost 250,000 manufacturing jobs last year, and Germany is losing 10,000-15,000 net manufacturing jobs a month.
insights.speaker: Sander Tordoir
insights.so_what: European industrial job losses are driving the political shift on China.
insights.quote: Germany is bleeding between 10 and 15,000 manufacturing net jobs a month.

insights.claim: In the latest German industry chamber survey, 66% of companies report growing competition with China as a major concern, and 83% of German manufacturing firms do.
insights.speaker: Sander Tordoir
insights.so_what: Chinese competition is now a broad-based German corporate concern.

insights.claim: China has generated about 6-7% of GDP growth from net exports in recent years after its real estate collapse, while Germany lost about 4% of GDP in net exports as it was pushed out of China and third markets.
insights.speaker: Sander Tordoir
insights.so_what: China's export-led growth is a direct drag on German GDP.

insights.claim: Tordoir says US Trump-2 tariffs were a 'footnote' in diverting Chinese overcapacity to Europe, because the North American market for Chinese machines, clean tech and cars was already closed under Trump 1 and Biden.
insights.speaker: Sander Tordoir
insights.so_what: Europe's China problem is structural and would persist even without US tariffs.
insights.quote: my maybe surprising answer is that the US tariffs were footnote in this

insights.claim: China is ripping European technology out of its wind energy infrastructure with tenders requiring full localization.
insights.speaker: Sander Tordoir
insights.so_what: European wind OEMs face exclusion from the Chinese market.

insights.claim: Germany's trade deficit with China has tripled and is heading toward about 2.5% of German GDP.
insights.speaker: Sander Tordoir
insights.so_what: Rising dependence on Chinese imports deepens economic security concerns.
insights.quote: Germany's trade deficit with with China has tripled

insights.claim: Tordoir expects China to let the renminbi appreciate a couple of percent a year nominally, which won't offset inflation differentials or meaningfully curb export-led growth.
insights.speaker: Sander Tordoir
insights.so_what: Don't expect currency adjustment to resolve the imbalance.

insights.claim: A Plaza Accord-style deal is off the table because China blames the Plaza Accord for Japan's lost decades; a more plausible deal is the EU holding back trade measures in exchange for renminbi appreciation.
insights.speaker: Sander Tordoir
insights.so_what: Multilateral FX deals with China are unlikely.

insights.claim: Tordoir says China now unequivocally meets the criteria to be designated a currency manipulator by the US Treasury, yet the US is missing in action on currency diplomacy.
insights.speaker: Sander Tordoir
insights.so_what: The US is ceding G7 currency leadership to Europe.

themes.theme: Chinese FDI and Europe's industrial policy

insights.claim: Chinese FDI in Europe is about 10-20 billion a year (currency unstated), concentrated in autos and batteries, mainly BYD and CATL plants in Hungary, Spain and to some extent Germany.
insights.speaker: Sander Tordoir
insights.so_what: Chinese auto/battery plants in Europe are the main FDI vector.

insights.claim: Past Chinese M&A like the KUKA robotics deal (now reportedly 90% localized in China) and Nexperia are seen as strategic catastrophes, and Italy, the Netherlands, Germany, France and the UK have all blocked Chinese semiconductor investment in the last five years.
insights.speaker: Sander Tordoir
insights.so_what: Chinese semiconductor M&A in Europe is effectively closed.

insights.claim: The draft Industrial Accelerator Act would require large FDI over 100 million from dominant-market countries (effectively China) to meet conditions such as 1% of global revenue in EU R&D, half European workers and around 30% European-sourced components; the Commission wants four of six conditions, Parliament all six.
insights.speaker: Sander Tordoir
insights.so_what: Chinese automakers' EU plants will face local-content and R&D conditions.

insights.claim: Chinese firms have every incentive to open low-local-content final assembly 'screwdriver' plants in Europe to jump the 350,000 hybrid quota, making FDI conditions essential.
insights.speaker: Sander Tordoir
insights.so_what: Expect Chinese assembly investment in Europe to rise as a quota workaround.

insights.claim: A key fight under the Industrial Accelerator Act is whether the UK, Turkey and Morocco qualify as 'made in Europe'; the UK may have to extend EU car tariffs on China in exchange for local-content status.
insights.speaker: Sander Tordoir
insights.so_what: UK trade policy may converge with EU China tariffs.

themes.theme: Transatlantic relations and Europe's network strategy

insights.claim: Tordoir says Europe could not push back on Liberation Day tariffs largely because of its hard security dependence on the US, but expects that dependence to fall sharply by decade-end as European defense spending surges.
insights.speaker: Sander Tordoir
insights.so_what: Rising EU defense spending will rebalance transatlantic leverage over time.

insights.claim: Liberation Day and Turnberry tariffs have shaved at most about 0.4% off EU GDP, so Tordoir counsels Europe to be patient and wait for the US debate to resolve.
insights.speaker: Sander Tordoir
insights.so_what: US tariff damage to EU GDP is modest and largely already done.

insights.claim: The transatlantic trade relationship is about $1.6 trillion a year and more balanced including services; Europe imports AI and cloud services from the US, making decoupling neither smart nor feasible.
insights.speaker: Sander Tordoir
insights.so_what: US tech services exports to Europe are structurally entrenched.

insights.claim: Harrell describes a US debate between a Western Hemisphere 'Donroe doctrine' sphere-of-influence view and Rush Doshi/Kurt Campbell's 'allied scale' approach of common external tariffs with lower internal barriers, and expects post-Trump policy to revert toward traditional alliances.
insights.speaker: Peter Harrell
insights.so_what: Allied-scale trade policy could return under a future administration.

insights.claim: A Bertelsmann Foundation study finds the EU's new and deepened FTAs (India, Indonesia, Mercosur etc.) add only about 0.6% to EU GDP over the medium term.
insights.speaker: Sander Tordoir
insights.so_what: FTAs are strategically useful but economically marginal.

insights.claim: Tordoir frames Europe's emerging strategy as 'network sovereignty' — a Carney-style middle-power approach sharing value chains with partners — versus US bullying power and Chinese autarky.
insights.speaker: Sander Tordoir
insights.so_what: Expect EU deals bundling trade, critical minerals and defense with partners.

insights.claim: Tordoir expects the hawkish EU China line to persist through upcoming elections because it is backed by unions and businesses, though far-right and far-left parties are largely pro-China; sovereignty and rearmament will advance while Draghi-style market reforms erode — a 'K-shaped' policy outcome.
insights.speaker: Sander Tordoir
insights.so_what: Defense spending likely rises while EU growth reforms stall.

insights.claim: Harrell argues that over a 10-15 year horizon decoupling costs of several trillion dollars amount to only a couple of percentage points of combined US-EU GDP, and are lower still if done at allied scale, with supply chains moving to places like Mexico and Malaysia.
insights.speaker: Peter Harrell
insights.so_what: Gradual decoupling is economically manageable and favors alternative manufacturing hubs.

insights.claim: Harrell expects US Treasury to expand outbound investment restrictions on AI and add Chinese biotech, while barriers to Chinese car investment in the US remain.
insights.speaker: Peter Harrell
insights.so_what: US capital flows into Chinese AI and biotech face new limits.
